video.title: Electrospun PLA: How Surface Treatment Changed the Experiment
video.media_license: CC BY 4.0, 2020 authors / Surface & Coatings Technology
video.visual_thesis: Actual 2020 electrospun PLA fibre-mat study; Figure 1, original SEM Figure 5, AFM Figure 6, FTIR Figure 7 and Table 3. No figures from the separate 2021 PLA foil/aluminium adhesion experiment.

headline: A FIBRE MAT.
NOT A FILM.
chapters.narration: This is an electrospun PLA scaffold, not a packaging film. The question was whether a carefully modified surface could reduce bacterial colonization without losing its fibrous architecture.

headline: ELECTRIC
FIELD → FIBRES
chapters.narration: Electrospinning turns a polymer solution into fine fibres. The source paper used a high voltage needle and a collecting drum. This moving strand is an explanatory schematic, not filmed laboratory footage.

headline: THIRTY SECONDS
OF PLASMA
chapters.narration: A brief radiofrequency plasma treatment generated reactive surface sites. Thirty seconds was selected for subsequent grafting after the authors examined wettability and hydroperoxide formation.

headline: THE FIBRES
ARE REAL
chapters.narration: The original scanning electron micrographs show the untreated mat, plasma treated fibres and both acid grafted preparations. These are the images of this scaffold experiment, with its own three micrometre scale bars.

headline: SURFACE
TOPOGRAPHY
chapters.narration: Atomic force microscopy revealed differences in surface roughness and morphology after treatment. These are the actual five sample conditions reported in Figure six, not illustrations borrowed from a different polymer study.

headline: LOOK AT
THE SPECTRA
chapters.narration: The FTIR spectra compare untreated PLA, plasma treated fibres, both grafted mats and the neat acids. Spectral changes support surface modification, but one absorption band by itself is not a full chemical proof.

headline: BACTERIAL
COLONIES
chapters.narration: In the paper's bacterial colonization assessment, grafted samples were scored zero in all three entries for both Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. These are in vitro test scores, not an infection cure.

headline: THE CLAIM
HAS LIMITS
chapters.eyebrow: SURFACE SCIENCE / NOT A CLINICAL IMPLANT
chapters.narration: This experiment links surface treatment to the measured behaviour of electrospun fibres and bacterial growth under laboratory conditions. It does not establish the long term safety or effectiveness of an implanted scaffold.
